> **What this case shows** — a single periodogram of a short EEG segment is *noisy*, and
> its variance does not shrink as you record longer. The **multitaper method** fixes this:
> it passes the signal through a family of orthogonal **DPSS (Slepian) tapers**, takes a
> periodogram through each, and averages them — trading a little frequency resolution for a
> large drop in variance and controlled spectral leakage. On real eyes-closed occipital EEG
> the ecosystem's `eegMultitaper` computes this robust spectrum, and it is **alpha-dominated**
> (peak at **10.5 Hz**, 46 % of the 0–45 Hz power in the 8–13 Hz band). And it is built
> correctly: its DPSS tapers reproduce `scipy.signal.windows.dpss` to **~6e-14**, its full
> PSD reproduces an independent scipy+numpy reconstruction to **~1e-10**, and it agrees with
> the field-standard **MNE** `psd_array_multitaper` in structure (correlation **0.99**).

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for a low-variance power spectrum: `eegMultitaper(pe, bandwidth)` → read the
PSD from `metadata(pe)$multitaper_psd` over `metadata(pe)$multitaper$frequencies`.
**Way of thinking** — the tapers *are* the method. `bandwidth` (the time-bandwidth product
NW) sets the variance/resolution trade-off; the number of usable tapers is `2·NW − 1`. More
tapers = less variance, broader smoothing.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioEEG::eegMultitaper()`; `multitaperCoherence()` for the
low-variance cross-spectrum.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed occipital EEG (eegmmidb S001R02, O1), `eegMultitaper` reproduces
`scipy.signal.windows.dpss` (~6e-14) and an independent scipy+numpy multitaper reconstruction
(~1e-10) to machine precision, agrees with MNE `psd_array_multitaper` in structure (corr
0.99), and the spectrum peaks at the 10.5 Hz alpha rhythm.

## Question & goal

**The question is whether the ecosystem builds the multitaper spectrum from the right pieces
— the DPSS tapers and their average — the way the field-standard tools do.** A multitaper
PSD is only as good as its tapers (the DPSS eigenvectors) and its normalization. The goal is
to validate both against `scipy` and `MNE`, and to read the occipital spectrum.

## Challenge & approach

The non-adaptive multitaper PSD is **P(f) = (1/K)·Σₖ |FFT(x·hₖ)|² / sr**, where `hₖ` are the
first K DPSS tapers for a chosen time-bandwidth NW. We compute it with `eegMultitaper`, check
the tapers against `scipy.signal.windows.dpss`, rebuild the PSD from scratch with scipy+numpy,
and compare the shape to `MNE`.

```
O1 EEG → eegMultitaper(NW=4, 7 tapers) → PSD
                    DPSS tapers  vs scipy.signal.windows.dpss        (machine precision)
                    full PSD     vs scipy+numpy reconstruction        (machine precision)
                    full PSD     vs MNE psd_array_multitaper          (structure, corr 0.99)
```

## Data

**eegmmidb — EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (PhysioNet)**: subject S001, baseline run
**R02 (eyes-closed)**, occipital channel **O1**, first 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked
PhysioExperiment the sibling [`eeg-wavelet-alpha`](../eeg-wavelet-alpha-eegmmidb/index.qmd)
case reads. Details in [`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

*How to read this:* the left panel is the **validation** (three computations of the same

| Quantity | This reproduction | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Dominant frequency | **10.5 Hz** (alpha) | — |
| Alpha-band power fraction (0–45 Hz) | **0.46** | — |
| DPSS tapers vs `scipy.signal.windows.dpss` | **6e-14** | 0 (machine precision) |
| PSD vs independent scipy+numpy reconstruction | **1e-10** | 0 (machine precision) |
| PSD correlation vs MNE `psd_array_multitaper` | **0.99** | 1 (structure) |
| MNE / op scale (one-sided factor) | **2.00** | convention |

The tapers and the PSD are exact against `scipy`; the shape matches MNE up to its one-sided
factor-of-2. Values trace to
[`artifacts/multitaper_summary.csv`](artifacts/multitaper_summary.csv) and the full spectrum
(op, scipy, MNE) in [`artifacts/multitaper_psd.csv`](artifacts/multitaper_psd.csv).

## Conclusion

The ecosystem's multitaper spectrum is built from the correct DPSS tapers — exact against
`scipy` — and the same average MNE computes, up to a one-sided normalization. The transferable
takeaway: **use multitaper when you need a low-variance spectrum of a short or noisy segment;
set `bandwidth` (NW) to trade variance against resolution; validate the tapers against the
field-standard, and remember that PSD normalization (one-sided vs two-sided) is a convention —
compare shapes and correlations, not absolute power, across tools.**

## Open questions

- `eegMultitaper` is the **non-adaptive** multitaper (equal-weight taper average). The
  **adaptive** form (Thomson's iterative eigenvalue weighting, MNE's `adaptive=TRUE`)
  down-weights the leakier tapers and tightens the estimate near sharp peaks; and a multitaper
  **cross**-spectrum gives a low-variance coherence (`multitaperCoherence`, also implemented).
  Extending this to the adaptive PSD — and pinning the one-sided normalization to MNE's
  exactly — would turn a validated estimator into a connectivity tool. *Documented, not
  escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| multitaper PSD (robust spectrum) | `eegMultitaper()` | PhysioEEG |
| multitaper coherence (low-variance) | `multitaperCoherence()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| Morlet time-frequency (when timing matters) | `waveletTransform()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| the aperiodic 1/f background | `eegAperiodic()` | PhysioEEG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **bandwidth** — the time-bandwidth product **NW** (here 4); larger NW → more tapers, lower
  variance, broader frequency smoothing. The number of usable tapers is `2·NW − 1` (7 here).
- **n_tapers** — override the `2·NW − 1` default to use fewer tapers (less smoothing).
- **normalization** — the op returns a two-sided-convention PSD (positive frequencies not
  doubled); MNE's one-sided PSD is ~2× — compare shapes across tools, not absolute magnitudes.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioEEG)

mt  <- eegMultitaper(pe, bandwidth = 4)          # NW = 4 -> 7 DPSS tapers
psd <- S4Vectors::metadata(mt)$multitaper_psd    # power[frequency, channel]
f   <- S4Vectors::metadata(mt)$multitaper$frequencies
f[which.max(psd[, 1])]                            # 10.5 Hz -- the alpha peak

# DPSS tapers reproduce scipy.signal.windows.dpss (~6e-14); PSD ~ MNE psd_array_multitaper
# in structure (corr 0.99), up to a one-sided factor-of-2.
```
